notes: The catalogue names the Pi's header port GPIO_HEADER; I used 'GND' and 'GPIO17' as header-pin names on rpi1, as the task instructions suggest. GND is physical pin 9 and GPIO17 is physical pin 11, as in the image.

The breadboard uses the catalogue naming where bank 't' is rows a-e. The image shows rows a-e as the lower half, so both buzzer legs and wire ends go in row a: columns 15 (negative) and 18 (positive).
The buzzer's port 1 is assumed to be positive and port 2 negative. The black wire and black leg are on column 15 (GND). The purple leg is on column 18 (GPIO 17).
The tutorial's jumper wires are jumper-wire per the matched parts list, though the Pi end would physically need a female connector.
